rawInput.transcript: Slot canyon tour. The light beams come down through the sandstone around midday. Our group had to book months ahead. The Navajo guide explained flash floods carved these curves over thousands of years and that the canyon closes when rain falls anywhere upstream. Sand pours over the edges like waterfalls when the wind picks up. Photographers used to haul tripods in on special tours but those ended a few years back.
rawInput.operatorNotes: Nobody named any sources on this one — no plaques in the canyon.

rawInput.transcript: Ranger station briefing. Kilauea is one of the most active shield volcanoes on Earth. The ranger discussed effusive versus explosive eruption regimes, tholeiitic basalt composition, the distinction between pahoehoe and a'a lava textures, summit caldera collapse during the 2018 lower East Rift Zone eruption, and how the USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory instruments deformation with tiltmeters and GNSS. Halema'uma'u crater roughly doubled in size in 2018.
rawInput.operatorNotes: This got very technical. Audience is families with kids.

rawInput.transcript: Tour intake numbers from the guide and the exhibit hall: dam completed in 1935, two years ahead of schedule. It is 726.4 feet tall and 1,244 feet across the crest. About 3.25 million cubic yards of concrete in the dam itself, enough to pave a two-lane highway from San Francisco to New York, the panel claims. Seventeen turbines generate around 4 billion kilowatt-hours a year serving roughly 1.3 million people. Lake Mead, the reservoir, is the largest in the U.S. by capacity. 96 workers died during construction per the memorial, though none are buried in the concrete — the guide was emphatic that's a myth. The dam was dedicated by FDR in September 1935.

rawInput.operatorNotes: Sorry, I just left the recorder running. There's maybe a lesson about Route 66 roadside culture and Cadillac Ranch in there somewhere.

rawInput.transcript: Walking the grounds with guide Lupe. She calls Mission San Jose 'la Reina de las Misiones' — the queen of the missions — founded in 1720 by Fray Antonio Margil de Jesus. The famous Rosa's Window, la Ventana de Rosa, is carved limestone from about 1775, considered the finest piece of Spanish colonial ornamentation in the country per the park brochure. Lupe explained the mission was a self-contained pueblo — 'aqui vivian unas trescientas personas,' around three hundred people lived here — with granary, mill and defensive walls. It's part of the San Antonio Missions UNESCO World Heritage Site designated in 2015.

End of Route 66 sign on the pier. The pier opened in 1909. The Looff Hippodrome carousel building is a National Historic Landmark from 1916. Pacific Park's Ferris wheel is solar-powered, the placard says the world's first. The 'End of the Trail' sign is technically a replica installed in 2009 for the route's 83rd anniversary.

rawInput.transcript: Ballpark tour. Fenway opened in April 1912, the oldest MLB park still in use. The Green Monster left-field wall is 37 feet 2 inches tall; the manual scoreboard inside it still gets updated by hand. The lone red seat in the right-field bleachers marks Ted Williams' 502-foot home run from 1946, the longest measured homer hit at Fenway per the tour guide. Pesky's Pole down the right field line is 302 feet from home plate.

location.name: Statue of Liberty, New York Harbor

rawInput.transcript: Ferry deck notes. Our guide today said the Statue of Liberty was a gift from Spain, delivered in 1920 to celebrate the end of the First World War. He said the sculptor was Pablo Bartoli and that the statue is solid bronze, which is why it's green. The torch, he said, has always been closed to visitors.
rawInput.operatorNotes: Use ONLY what the guide said — this is a 'guide said' style piece. Do not correct him from other sources.

rawInput.transcript: Bison range drive with a private guide. The island hosts one of the oldest managed bison herds in the country, started in 1893 with 12 animals barged across the lake. Each fall the park runs a bison roundup open to the public. The Great Salt Lake's salinity means only brine shrimp and brine flies thrive; millions of migrating birds feed on them. Fielding Garr Ranch on the island ran continuously from 1848 to 1981.
